The part every other resource skips 1461 items · 279 lessons

What you've forgotten by now

Reading a lesson is the weakest thing you can do with it. Retrieving it cold, a few days later, is the strongest — g ≈ 0.50–0.61, and the effect grows the longer you leave it. This page exists because that second thing needs a schedule and the first one doesn't.

Due today

Confidence first, before you look — afterwards it's contaminated by hindsight and measures nothing. Answer out loud or on paper; recognising a right answer is far easier than producing one, and this only works if you produce it.

◔

Calibration

The useful number is not how often you were right. It's how often you were certain and wrong — the cell a fluent explanation manufactures, because coherent prose reads as comprehension. That is the one thing you cannot detect by rereading.

Confident (4–5) — and right that often
Unsure (1–3) — and right that often
Verdict —
☰

Every node, and where it stands

Shaky means you got it right the same day you read it, which proves nothing. Known means you got it right on a later day. Mastered needs ≥90% across two or more later days — the gate exists because a wall of green for material that was fluent for ten minutes is this design's most likely way to lie to you.
